objective: Replace the apps/server placeholder with a Fastify server that implements every endpoint and SSE event in the game API contract below, so a player can play a full game as White or Black against the sparring bot: legal-move enforcement on the server (chess.js is the authority), takebacks, resign, game-over detection with result and endReason, the bot's reply pushed over SSE within 2 s (NFR-3), and finished and abandoned games saved as PGN in SQLite (FR-5, IR-7). The server also loads both repertoire files at startup and exits with a clear message if one is missing or does not parse (issue #6 scope addition, needed later by FR-6a/FR-19).
negative: Do not edit packages/**, apps/web, docs, config, .github, root files or the lockfile. Anything needed there goes in contract_gaps (e.g. a missing export, a contract change).
No new dependencies (Fastify's raw reply is enough for SSE; node:sqlite for storage). If one seems unavoidable, stop and report it in contract_gaps.
No network calls to Lichess from tests. Never write a token anywhere.
No tutor/Claude code yet (that is #7); no tutor events in GameEvent.
rubric: Tests written first, recorded red then green, covering: new game as White and as Black (bot moves first over SSE); legal move -> 200 and bot_move event; illegal/malformed move -> 400; wrong turn / bot thinking / not playing -> 409; unknown id -> 404; takeback after bot reply returns to the player's turn with two plies removed, and 409 when there is nothing to undo; resign; checkmate and a draw rule end the game with the right result/endReason and game_over event; first SSE message is state; abandoned-on-new-game and the PGN saved for finished and abandoned games (read back from the store); missing or unparsable repertoire file -> clear startup error naming the file; empty LICHESS_TOKEN -> engine-only bot without throwing.
Real WASM engine test: bot reply under 2000 ms (NFR-3).
